evidence.mission_note: This is a Porsche Cayman, which is on the active exclusions and deferred to 2027-28, and its likely hammer is far beyond the roughly $25k all-in target for the needed manual daily. It is interesting only as a future keeper, which conflicts with the current cash-preservation strategy.
evidence.rationale: The listing firmly establishes identity: the VIN matches the photographed window sticker, it is a 2006 Cayman S with a six-speed manual and Sport Chrono, and it has a 1-owner Carfax snapshot with no reported accidents. Photos show a very clean exterior and interior, fresh tires claimed from September 2026, and a dry, corrosion-free rear underside. Observed limitations are that the borescope examined only cylinder 6 from the top side, and that the Carfax lists a single service record across 20 years on a car the seller says saw little use for about 15 years. Open items are the contents of the 'service records', a DME over-rev report, and any dated coolant, brake fluid, AOS or water-pump work. Low mileage does not substitute for these time-based items. The expected hammer for an 11k-mile one-owner S sits at or above the $32.5k–$40.5k fair-value band, well outside the stated near-term budget. The model is also currently on the buyer's exclusion list.
evidence.next_action: Before the Sunday close, confirm whether Porsche is reopened as a keeper purchase; if so, ask the seller for scans of all service records, a DME over-rev report, and access for a mobile PPI with a full six-cylinder borescope.
